newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Shares tumble, mark up as EMU delay possible.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Shares tumble, mark up as EMU delay possible.

text.p: European bourses tumbled on Friday as all attention focused on increasingly shaky prospects for European monetary union, dented by the row between Bonn and the Bundesbank and the possibility that France's opposition socialists could win Sunday's parliamentary elections.
Wall Street's weak start also weighed on Europe's major bourses, which ended flat or well down on the day.
The mark and dollar benefited in turn from the increasing perception that economic and monetary union (EMU) could be delayed.
Initially investors bought the dollar as a safe haven. Later the mark gained support as the view took hold that it may remain a strong currency for longer if the 1999 EMU start date slips.

Markets have been thrown into disarray by the political storm over Bonn's intention to revalue its gold in an attempt to qualify for EMU, coupled with the increasing possibility the opposition socialists might win power in France's National Assembly.
Both developments pose serious question marks over future European economic integration.

On the French elections, James McKay, international economist at Painwebber, said a clear win for the opposition Socialists, who favour a flexible interpretation of the economic criteria for joining EMU, would spook European markets.
"If the Socialists take an absolute majority - that would be detrimental to markets...We could see a delay or abandonment to the EMU project," he said.
